audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Riven, Akshan, Akshan, Akshan, Skill, Akshan, Riven] and rows 1-6 of it match this page's own why text exactly. The chart and the explanation rendered opposite answers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Akshan's Q was called 'Going Rogue' in three places and his passive shot was called 'Dirty Hands (W)'. Heroic Swing's cooldown was given as 'roughly 16 seconds unleveled'.
audit.why: Riot data: Q is Avengerang (9/8/7/6/5s, 850 range, a boomerang that damages out and back), W is Going Rogue (the camouflage/Scoundrel ability), and the passive is Dirty Fighting (an extra reduced-damage shot per attack, plus a shield every third hit). Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 — 18s at rank 1, not 16.
audit.corrected: Real names used throughout, and the punish window stated as Heroic Swing's true 18s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most punishable cooldown was mis-stated by two seconds.
audit.why: Heroic Swing at rank 1 is 18s — a longer free window than the page claimed, which changes when you are allowed to walk up.
audit.corrected: mid now states 18 seconds at rank 1.

audit.why: The revive interaction (killing Akshan's Scoundrel resurrects his dead ally) is already stated in late and is correct per Riot's W text.

edits.before: At Level 1 you have Q poke and auto weaves but no lockdown — Akshan answers every step-up with ranged autos and his passive camouflage lets him duck out after poking and reset your read on him. Take the small trades at Q-tip range and don't over-commit your E shield before W is online. Level 2 is your first real window: W comes up and you can bait his Heroic Swing grapple by faking an engage, then E-dash in the moment he swings away and land W-stun into your full Q chain before he lands. The problem is Levels 3-5: Akshan's sustained ranged poke with Going Rogue bullets will drain you faster than you can heal it back in a pure farming lane, so you need to force decisive all-ins rather than trade chip for chip — he wins every war of attrition.
edits.after: At Level 1 you have Q poke and auto weaves but no lockdown — Akshan answers every step-up with ranged autos and Dirty Fighting's extra shot, which also shields him every third hit on you. Take the small trades at Q-tip range and don't over-commit your E shield before W is online. Level 2 is your first real window: W comes up and you can bait his Heroic Swing grapple by faking an engage, then E-dash in the moment he swings away and land W-stun into your full Q chain before he lands. The problem is Levels 3-5: Akshan's sustained Avengerang poke drains you faster than you can heal it back in a pure farming lane, so you need to force decisive all-ins rather than trade chip for chip — he wins every war of attrition.

edits.before: This is his sustained pressure window. Akshan's Heroic Swing lets him dodge your Q dashes by grappling to a jungle tree or minion and re-entering at an awkward angle, burning your cooldowns and trading back on his terms. Never extend a half-committed Q chain if you can see his E is available — either commit the full pattern or don't step up. Track Heroic Swing's cooldown (roughly 16 seconds unleveled): the instant it's down, Q-steer through his poke bullets to close distance, W-stun him in place, and finish the three-Q chain. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile extends your melee range and Wind Slash threatens an execute, but his Comeuppance (R) charges up a long-range shot that kills you at half HP if you stall — so once you hit 6, force the fight immediately rather than letting him back you into an R angle.
edits.after: This is his sustained pressure window. Akshan's Heroic Swing lets him dodge your Q dashes by grappling to terrain and re-entering at an awkward angle, burning your cooldowns and trading back on his terms. Never extend a half-committed Q chain if you can see his E is available — either commit the full pattern or don't step up. Track Heroic Swing (18s at rank 1): the instant it's down, Q-steer past his Avengerang to close distance, W-stun him in place, and finish the three-Q chain. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile extends your melee range and Wind Slash threatens an execute, but his Comeuppance (R) charges a long-range shot that kills you at half HP if you stall — so once you hit 6, force the fight immediately rather than letting him back you into an R angle.

edits.before: Once you complete Immortal Shieldbow your shield absorbs his burst burst pattern, and your Wind Slash execute closes out any trade he tries to extend at range.
edits.after: Once your second item lands, your E shield absorbs his burst pattern and Wind Slash closes out any trade he tries to extend at range from a grapple.
